title: Payroll tempo band projection and price-tilt playbook (2026)
body:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to align payroll tempo bands (FTE cadence), near-term headcount moves, and a simple price-tilt sensitivity that maps token price changes to hiring actions for Q2–Q4 2026. Not a finalized deck — working assumptions called out below.

Background/context:
- We expect workload mix shifts with more embeddings and reranking traffic vs pure generation through H2 2026. This reduces average tokens per request but increases concurrency.
- Short-term runway pressure + sales pipeline uncertainty means we should be able to flex ~10–20% of non-customer-facing headcount within 8–12 weeks.
- Objective: define tempo bands so finance + eng can proactively call hiring/moratorium triggers tied to token price movement and GPU cost shocks.

Key definitions (tempo bands):
- Baseline band (B): steady-state hiring to meet product roadmap (current org chart). Target utilization cushion = 12%
- Ramp band (R): planned growth hires (onboarding window 6–12 weeks). Adds +8–12% FTE headroom
- Surge band (S): temporary contractors / slow-rolling offers / hiring pause mitigators. Can add up to +20% capacity short-term but at higher cost per effective FTE

Assumptions (core):
- Avg cost per FTE (fully loaded): $170k/year (engineering), $120k/year (non-eng). Use blended $150k for mixed pools.
- GPU spot baseline run-rate: $0.80/hr/GPU; reserve committed price: $0.45/hr/GPU.
- Tokens per month baseline (Mar2026): 5.5B tokens. Token revenue/unit (hosted): $0.00008/token (current list)
- Variable infra cost per token (model/op) baseline: $0.000035/token (includes caching benefits)
- Target gross margin on route gates: 42% at baseline token price and current mix

Simple sensitivity table (excerpt):
(rounded numbers, for quick decisioning)
Scenario | token price | rev/month | infra cost/month | gross margin | implied FTE gap (vs baseline)
Central   | $0.00008  | $440k     | $193k            | 44%          | 0 FTE
Price -10%| $0.000072 | $396k     | $193k            | 38%          | -6 FTE (defer hires)
Price -20%| $0.000064 | $352k     | $193k            | 31%          | -14 FTE (freeze + contract augmentation)
Price +10%| $0.000088 | $484k     | $193k            | 60%          | +4 FTE (accelerate hires)

Notes on the table:
- Revenue = tokens * token price (5.5B * price).
- Infra cost held flat for short shocks (we assume caching and batching keep infra steady within 8 weeks). Longer shocks vary infra and change math.
- Implied FTE gap uses blended FTE fully-loaded cost and a 12-month smoothing (i.e., hiring impact amortized).

Payroll tempo band mapping (operational):
- If price delta <= -5% sustained for 3 consecutive weeks -> shift from Ramp (R) -> Baseline (B): pause non-critical requisitions, move open offers to deferred (90d). Activate surge bench prep (contract scopes).
- If price delta between -5% and -15% -> freeze hiring for non-customer success and non-sales engineering roles; re-evaluate within 6 weeks.
- If price drop > -15% or multi-factor (price + spot GPU > +25%) -> declare 'conservation posture': move to Surge band for contractors, reduce discretionary spend.
- If price increases +8% for 4 weeks and pipeline conversion improving -> move to Ramp, accelerate up to 50% of pending offers.

Headcount snapshot (work-in-progress):
- Baseline FTE (Mar 2026): 150 total (Engineering 80, Product 20, Sales+CS 25, Ops/Fin+Legal 25)
- Tempo band targets (delta from baseline):
  - Ramp band target (R): +12 FTE (engineering heavy: +8 eng, +2 product, +2 ops)
  - Surge band target (S): +20 FTE equivalent via contractors (mix: 14 eng-equivalent contractors, 6 infra ops) at ~1.9x cost per FTE hour

Cost math examples (quick):
- Adding 1 eng FTE: $170k/yr -> monthly burn delta ~ $14.2k
- Adding 10 contractor eng-equivalents (S band): assume $320k annualized cost per equivalent -> monthly burn ~ $266k

Operational actions & runbook (what finance does vs hiring manager):
- Monitor: daily token price metric + weekly blended margin (automated dashboard).
- Finance: run sensitivity update each Monday; escalate to GTM/CEO if margin < 30% or runway delta > 8 weeks vs plan.
- Hiring managers: maintain "offer readiness" list (offers that can be rescinded or rapidly accepted) and contractor brief templates.
- Eng leadership: keep two small technical task forces ready for rapid contractor onboarding (security checklist + infra quotas).

Open questions / risks (working):
- How quickly does directionally-lower token price reduce infra cost in practice? (caching/kv improvements may lag).
- Contract risk: contractor ramp time often 3–6 weeks for meaningful throughput in infra/serving runtime work.
- Sales feedback loop: if we pause hiring, will SLOs for enterprise integrations slip and cause churn? Need CS-run tradeoff matrix.
- Headcount morale impact of offer deferrals — must coordinate with People Ops to calibrate communication.

Next steps & todo (owner tags):
- Ayesha: wire up an automated weekly sensitivity sheet (pull token volume + price + infra spot prices) -> due 2026-04-09.
- Marta: draft contractor bench rubric (rates, security, oncall coverage) -> due 2026-04-16.
- Daniel: surface a CS churn-impact forecast for 60/90/180 day hiring pauses -> due 2026-04-12.
- Liam: work with infra to define a 6-week infra cost slippage curve matrix (how infra costs fall as batching/caching modifies token serving) -> due 2026-04-20.

Appendix: quick calculation snippets (copy/paste into a sheet)
- Revenue = tokens_month * token_price
- Gross margin = (Revenue - Infra_variable_cost) / Revenue
- Implied FTE_delta = round((Target_margin_gap * annual_revenue) / blended_FTE_cost)

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a light-weight working tool intended to be conservative on hiring and explicit on trigger windows. Please push back on the tempo band thresholds if you have data suggesting different lead times for roles.
- If we want a more rigorous model, next version should incorporate per-route granularity (generation vs embeddings vs rerank) and include a dynamic infra cost curve tied to GPU real-time pricing and observed batching gains.

-- end of working sheet --
